implementation_notes: Java absorbed CPS into CompletableFuture: thenApply and thenCompose chain continuations, each stage receiving the previous result, and the runtime threads the state machine. For genuinely stackless CPS in Java, a hand-written trampoline or an explicit continuation object is required, since Java has no first-class continuations. RecursiveCompletableFuture chains compose deeply without stack growth because each stage returns a new future rather than nesting a call - the same property CPS plus trampolining gives, delivered by the library.
idiom_name: CompletableFuture thenApply/thenCompose continuations; explicit state machine for hand-written CPS
pitfalls: thenApply with a blocking body runs on the completing thread and blocks the pool; use thenApplyAsync with an explicit executor when the work is CPU-bound.
exceptionally swallows the original into a CompletionException wrapper, so the catch block sees a different type than the thrower produced.
thenCompose (a function returning a future) and thenApply (a function returning a value) are easy to confuse: the wrong one produces a CompletableFuture<CompletableFuture<T>>.
